# Tim Dobermann

<p class="hero-role">Economist</p>

<p class="hero-affiliation">Director of Research &amp; Chief Economist, International Growth Centre<br>Research Fellow, London School of Economics</p>

<p class="hero-lede">I study how energy systems, climate change, and new technologies like AI reshape growth in developing economies, using field experiments, administrative data, and quantitative models.</p>

::: {.home-section .research-agenda}
<p class="section-kicker">Research agenda</p>

## Three questions

<p class="section-intro">My work asks how economies build productive capabilities, how the systems that supply energy actually function, and who is able to adapt when the climate changes.</p>

<div class="agenda-grid">
<div class="agenda-item">
<span class="agenda-number">01</span>
<h3>Climate adaptation and human capital</h3>
<p>How education and mobility determine who can adapt to a changing climate, and why climate damages fall so unequally across places.</p>
</div>
<div class="agenda-item">
<span class="agenda-number">02</span>
<h3>Energy markets and state capacity</h3>
<p>How contracts, prices, metering, and enforcement shape the reliability and affordability of electricity, and what that costs firms.</p>
</div>
<div class="agenda-item">
<span class="agenda-number">03</span>
<h3>Structural transformation and technology</h3>
<p>How industrial policy, artificial intelligence, and changing sectoral capabilities alter the path from poverty to prosperity.</p>
</div>
</div>
:::

<h3><a href="papers/human-capital-climate-mobility.html">Human Capital, Mobility, and the Unequal Effects of Climate Change</a></h3>
<p class="paper-authors">Tim Dobermann</p>
<p>Education lets people change sector and location when crop conditions worsen — but the places facing the largest damages invest least in it.</p>
</div>
<div class="featured-paper">
<p class="paper-meta">Working paper · Energy markets</p>
<h3><a href="papers/economic-costs-lopsided-ppas-pakistan.html">The Economic Costs of Lopsided Contracts</a></h3>
<p class="paper-authors">With Faraz Hayat and Sugandha Srivastav</p>
<p>A new database on Pakistan's power purchase agreements, and what asymmetric information and regulatory capture cost the wider economy.</p>
</div>
<div class="featured-paper">
<p class="paper-meta">Working paper · AI &amp; development</p>
<h3><a href="papers/ai-ladder-of-development.html">AI and the Ladder of Development</a></h3>
<p class="paper-authors">Tim Dobermann</p>
<p>Frontier AI can raise measured productivity while pulling labour toward weak-learning sectors — raising income now, capability growth later.</p>
</div>
<div class="featured-paper">
<p class="paper-meta">Field experiments · Pakistan</p>
<h3><a href="papers/pushing-on-a-string-pakistan.html">Pushing on a String?</a></h3>
<p class="paper-authors">With Robin Burgess, Michael Greenstone, Faraz Hayat, and Usman Naeem</p>
<p>Two randomised experiments run with government on how prices and norm-based enforcement change electricity payment and theft.</p>

<p class="section-kicker">From evidence to policy</p>

## Research that reaches the room where decisions are made

<p>The same questions arrive twice: once as an identification problem, once as a live policy choice. I work directly with finance and energy ministries on tariff design, subsidy reform, and growth strategy — which is also where the data, the institutional constraints, and the next research question come from.</p>

<p><a href="policy.html" class="text-link-arrow">Explore policy work →</a></p>
</div>
<dl class="engagement-rail">
<div class="engagement-rail-item">
<dt>Pakistan</dt>
<dd>Electricity tariffs, power purchase agreements, and tax reform, with the Ministries of Energy and Finance.</dd>
</div>
<div class="engagement-rail-item">
<dt>Ethiopia</dt>
<dd>National energy policy and evidence on metering, reliability, and firm performance.</dd>
</div>
<div class="engagement-rail-item">
<dt>Myanmar</dt>
<dd>The technical update of the National Electrification Plan and Yangon's urban growth.</dd>
</div>
</dl>
</div>
